links.reason: The verse says the hero marries five hundred women (மங்கையரை) and nothing about their being unmarried, so the claim that the couplet's bar on another's wife leaves room for them is supplied from outside the Tamil. A real contrast with பிறன்மனை, but the gains clause rests on that missing fact.

Both verses have a flower rain (பூமழை), but 1886 names no king's approach or offering to answer, and 1897 does not say whom the rain answers. The 'worship and its reception' pairing is the marker's reading, so the shared image is only stock decoration.

Both turn on a widow's plain greens (வால் அடகு / வேளை வெந்தை) and a refused rich food, and the contrast of rejecting it for the pyre versus taking it as tapas is real. It is not an incompatible claim, though; they are two women in two situations, so it is a parallel, not a tension.
links.text_issue: Line 4 of 354 is a repaired 8-half-line stanza.

links.reason: Both name desire as liquor (காமம் என்னும் மதுவினில் குளித்த / காமவெந் தேறல் மாந்தி), and the father/son contrast is available. But the image is stock, 'in time to leave it by choice' is not in 2729, and both verses are flagged uncertain, so pairing adds little.

175 is a poet's simile of shoots taking the form of women's hands and waists; it makes no claim about the body's worth, so Naladiyar 48's vultures and carcass do not contradict it. A topic contrast (body as beauty versus body as carrion) is not a tension, and 'a counter-voice that sees the beauty fading' is not in 175.

Both give a triad after refuge, but 201 says only discerning true things, knowledge and conduct (the Jain triad is a reading), while Manimekalai 30 has the three jewels as the object of refuge. The contrast of what one goes to versus what one holds is true but generic, and the number three is the whole link.

Both use darkness removed by clear sight (இருள்நீங்கி / தீவினை இருள்கள் போழும்). But the couplet does not say the sight is one's own as against a teacher's, so the 'teacher versus own sight' contrast is invented, and the gain to the Kural is an interpretive guess.

Both attach the elephant-fire hunger (குஞ்சரம் முழங்கு தீ / தந்தித் தீ) to a person, but they are two different people: the ascetic in 396 and Kayasandikai in the Manimekalai. 396 says only பாவம் வந்து அடைந்தது and does not exclude a former deed, so 'no deed in this life to explain it' is read in.
150 simply carries out the plan proposed in 149 (அத்திசை போவோம் answering சார்வோம்), which is plot sequence the graph already records. 'The long mourning ends with an act' is not in either verse.

993 is a simile (பிறப்பு உணர்ந்தவர் போல்) for a girl spurning kin's talk. Naladiyar 30 is about kin who come and go at birth and death like a bird leaving a tree, not about detachment from kin. The 'figure of speech' gain and the 'same withdrawal, opposite causes' reading rest on the marker's stretch.

Naladiyar 34 calls the body அரும்பெறல் யாக்கை and urges taking its fruit; 2749 gives the rarity a measure (the drifting pole and the yoke-hole, அரிதால் ... மானிடம் பெறலே). Each adds what the other lacks, a reason for using the body and a duty drawn from the rarity.

The envoys relay the enemy king's boast (சிறியோன் ... கோளரி ஒழிக்கலான்), so unsoftened speech is plausible against Kural 685. But the claim that the minister of 700 wants the youth angered is not in this verse, and the verse is flagged uncertain, so 'offence as chosen policy' is reconstructed.
links.text_issue: Sense flagged uncertain; the purpose rests on verses outside this packet.

links.reason: 1923 gives the lower hells' totals (49 layers, 84 lakh dwellings) and 1926 gives the first hell's thirteen levels and thirty lakh pits, which fits as part of the whole. It is one sage's continuous catalogue, though, so it reads as sequence, not as an answer or fulfilment.

324 has Vijayai blessing the child: நுன் பழம் பகை தவ நூறுவாய். 2329 has the women saying he has destroyed the enemy with all his sons (மக்களொடு எல்லாம் ... செற்றான்). That is a blessing and its public fulfilment, and the note says which is which.

1284 does not mention the drum offer; it is an appeal (வித்தி கேண்மையை விளைத்தி) whose speaker and addressee are uncertain even in the marker's note. Calling it a restatement of the 1275 prize is a plausible reading, but 'offered to Civakan in particular, before the cure' is not shown.
links.text_issue: Speaker/addressee ambiguous (நம்பி and கொற்ற வேந்தன் both named).

links.reason: Both treat pallor (பசலை / பசப்பு) as a surface that appears the moment contact ends, which is a good parallel. But 1187 is still hyperbole (அள்ளிக்கொள்வற்று), so the poem does not explain it as 'not exaggeration', and 'develops' imposes a dependence the texts do not show.

Both rest on 'he is within me' (உள்ளத்தார் / உள்ளத்துள்). They are two uses of one fact, not incompatible claims, and 1249 does not show her trapped by it, only laughing at the heart's search. 'Once consoled, now traps' is invented.

Both have a list of 'X-ஓ' guesses ending in கூற்றமோ, so the riddle form matches Kural 1085. But the epic's ten likenesses are stock eye-similes, and that the epic list is modelled on the couplet is a guess, so the 'gains' are speculative.

1181's king asking whether the war is of men, gods or both can be read as a reply to 1172 (தானவர் செருவன்றாயின்), but 1172's speaker is unnamed and the link is nine verses of plot apart. 'Answers the warning' is not shown by the Tamil.

Both verses choose a learned man as envoy, so they are a true parallel (கற்றவன் ... ஓதும் மாண்பினான்). But that both courts hold the same practice is one shared theme, and 'develops' does not fit two sides' separate counsels.

1946 hyperbolically says the city women's breasts turn back even seekers of release. 2651 shows a queen taking austerity. These are not incompatible claims, only a shared topic of women and renunciation, and the note's contrast is the marker's.

1017 asks whether she is a goddess's daughter, a Vidyadhara or an earthly woman and bids him judge; 1018 answers that no earth-woman has such form, so, if not a sky woman, the Vidyadhara king's daughter. The later verse answers the earlier by elimination, as the note says.

2291 says இமைத்திலன் of the warrior's fierce eye as the spear comes, which is exactly the test of Kural 775 (அழித்திமைப்பின் ஒட்டன்றோ). The epic adds the cost: he is pierced for keeping it. Both gains clauses are true.

The shared word is பொறி, but Kural 6 praises those who follow the one who quenched the senses, and 1818 describes Vijayai's penance. The verse has her friends take leave, eat and order the army out (என்றார்), not Vijayai commanding it. 'Ascetic control sits with worldly purpose' is the marker's reading.

Both call the body unreliable beneath its surface (பொள்ளல் இவ்வுடம்பு / தொளை பலவாய்). But the Naladiyar's bag turned inside out is more specific than 'hollow', and the verse's lines 2-3 are obscure, so 'driving an abdication' is the marker's inference.

Both put adultery's cost in suffering. But Naladiyar 84 has no blade, and 2871 gives no worldly penalty or hell, only துன்பம். So 'the same image of a blade' and 'a worldly punishment and a future one' in both are not in the Tamil.

139 has the king refuse to take a life to save his own, and 297 names the animal births from killing. The link depends on the story outside the packet that the king there is Yasodharan, and 139 does not name him. It is a reversal, not a tension.

1016 shows the portrait and 1019 shows him looking and Kaman taking aim. This is the next beat of the same scene, so it is plot sequence the graph records. The 'no meeting yet' remark is true but thin.

1340 reads the match as விதி (விதிதர வந்தது); 1359 has the hero depart with பொறி as his chariot. Different words, and 1359 names his own resolve (எழுந்தது உள்ளம்). So 'the same fate that makes the marriage carries him away' stretches the contrast.

UKK 365 burns இருவினை, two deeds, in meditation. NKK 165 says நாலிரு வினைகள், four-and-two, the eight kinds of deed, which is not the same count. So the note's 'two deeds' for both is wrong for 165, and 165 is a chapter-five verse about Vyalan and Mavyalan, not the work's end.

1921 says there are four destinies that turn souls and 1922 names them (நரகர் விலங்கு மனிதர் தேவர்). That is a clean listing, but the teaches line about the wheel carrying a soul into hell or heaven is not in either verse.

548 has Dharanan give the lore, a companion and a mountain after hearing the wish (இச்சை). Tirumanthiram 670 is about siddhis by yoga and Shakti's grace. Nothing in 548 says Nami wanted wealth, or that the lore is a siddhi, so the 'siddhis without yoga' contrast and its gains are not in the Tamil.

2902 is the reply to 2901's offer, and its refusal of heaven and release (துறக்கமும் வீடும் வேண்டேன்) for the brother's feet is the specific addition. That makes it a develops pair, not a tension, since the two claims do not conflict.

The Siddhar asks நட்டகல்லும் பேசுமோ; the epic has the shrine 'speak' (தெய்வம் தான் வாய்விட்டுரைத்தது) and the narrator calls it பட்டிமை, a man's trick. The epic shows what makes a stone speak, and the Siddhar's mockery supplies the doctrinal edge. Both gains hold.

1390 raises Kanaka Chitran's kin and 1392 has the younger brothers and kings join. Which side the brothers belong to is not clear in 1390, and 'spreads by loyalty rather than by order' is not in either. It is plot sequence.

Neelakesi 97 names 'the sin of killing' and 'the sin of eating flesh' and burns the beings in fire; Tirumanthiram 198 puts those who said கொல்லிடு குத்து in fire-mouthed hell. The first extends guilt to the eater, the second to the one who orders, and together they widen the chain. The note is accurate about both.

The friend asks him to say he will return (வருவீர் ஆகுதல் உரைமின்), and the lizard omen makes even lords turn back (நின்றாங்குப் பெயரும் கானம்). A turning-back omen suggests return, not that a promise is empty, and the last line is obscure. So the note's 'why it is empty' is the marker's reading.

723 is a real lion killed by Tivittan (அரி ... பிளந்து போழ்களாய்க் கிடந்தது). Tirumanthiram 2026's five lions are the senses. The shared word is the lion, with no common use, and the epic's lion is not symbolic, so both gains are stretched.

2929 says those who never ate after giving (கொடுத்துண்டு அறியாதார்) stand begging; Naladiyar 107 says begging at great gates is முன்னை வினை. The epic names the deed the quatrain leaves general, and the quatrain supplies the karmic frame the epic only implies.

160 says that if he understands outcomes arise from deeds, joy and companions follow. Siddhar 335 says the body is the enjoyment of deeds and that Siva's foot joins those who think of it. Neither says understanding is enough, nor that grace releases from deeds, so no incompatible claim is stated and the 'meets' gain is invented.

1425 has the king, in grief and anger (the Tamil gives words of despair, என்னை என்னா, not சினம்), choose a spell that sweeps up all living things. That is harm to the world, but the verse does not show his anger killing him, so it does not test 'தன்னையே கொல்லும் சினம்'. The gains rest on supplied anger.

420 has an announcer warn of an ill omen (பிள்ளை, a reading) and the herders go anyway. 415 gives only that an omen-reader spoke, not that the hunters ignored it. So 'both ignore the omen' is not in 415, and the bird word in 420 is uncertain.
links.text_issue: பிள்ளை in 420 is read as an omen-bird name; uncertain.

links.reason: Both give rage as fire (வெகுளி ... செந்தீ / ஒள்ளெரி கனல் மூட்டினான்), one in the eyes and one in the heart. Anger as fire is stock imagery, and 'two fires meeting' is the marker's thematic reading, not something the verses do together.
